title: Measurement architecture and sensor selection
text: The proposed platform architecture should be described through functions and interfaces before it is expressed as an enclosure. Observation, environmental management, physical control, computation, review and data storage have different timing, failure and service requirements. Their separation can be logical, electrical or physical; no single compartment arrangement is prescribed here.

pages.title: Measurement architecture without a fixed enclosure
text: The proposed platform architecture should be described through functions and interfaces before it is expressed as an enclosure. Observation, environmental management, physical control, computation, review and data storage have different timing, failure and service requirements. Their separation can be logical, electrical or physical; no single compartment arrangement is prescribed here.
## Define what crosses a boundary

An imaging subsystem should provide observations with configuration, timing and quality metadata. A control subsystem should expose permitted commands and confirmed states. An analysis subsystem should return derived values linked to exact inputs. These contracts let designers compare alternative mechanical layouts and computing arrangements without changing the meaning of a record.
## Design for coupling that cannot be eliminated

Heat from computation can change an optical assembly. A fan can introduce vibration. An illumination change can alter both image contrast and sample heating. Treating modules as separate boxes in a diagram does not remove these interactions. Integration testing should identify and quantify the couplings that matter to the selected measurement.

A candidate layout should therefore be assessed against measurement quality, access for service, contamination management, power, thermal behaviour and recovery. The strongest arrangement is the one that meets the chosen requirements with evidence. It need not be the most compact, the most sensor-rich or the one containing the newest processor.

pages.title: Optical geometry and spatial calibration
text: An imaging instrument measures a physical object through an optical projection. A zone diameter expressed in pixels becomes a length only when the relationship between the image and the relevant plate plane is established. Resolution, repeatability and accuracy describe different properties; a dense pixel array cannot substitute for a calibrated measurement chain.
## Define the measurement plane

The proposed reader should reference the plane at which zone boundaries are interpreted. A ruler attached to a raised lid can have a different scale from the agar surface under perspective imaging. Calibration therefore needs a traceable target at the intended plane, a declared working range and a check for local distortion across the field. Telecentric optics are a candidate for reducing magnification changes with depth, but their benefits must be weighed against field size, working distance and integration cost. [R15]
## Carry geometry into uncertainty

For an ideal uniform scale, diameter d equals pixel span p multiplied by scale s in millimetres per pixel. A first order independent uncertainty approximation is u(d)² = s²u(p)² + p²u(s)². Correlated terms must be included when the same images or reference features influence both quantities. This approximation does not cover all lens distortion or ambiguous biological edges. [R16]

The acceptance decision should use a measurement uncertainty budget and independent target checks. A successful camera self-test establishes instrument readiness; biological agreement still requires a separate study against the appropriate reference workflow.

pages.title: Illumination and image formation
text: Illumination is part of the measurement chain. A plate image records the combined effects of the light source, optical path, specimen, lens, sensor and processing pipeline. Changes in any of these can alter apparent contrast even when the underlying biological object is unchanged.
## Control the useful dimensions of light

The proposed reader should qualify source geometry, intensity stability, spectral content and spatial uniformity. Reflected and transmitted light can answer different questions. Oblique illumination may reveal texture while making a boundary appear different from its appearance under a standard reading geometry. A multimode acquisition should therefore identify the mode in each observation rather than merge images without provenance.
## Preserve linearity where it matters

Automatic enhancement, tone mapping and local contrast processing can improve appearance while changing quantitative relationships. A measurement pipeline should declare which processing stages are permitted and retain enough original data to investigate their effect. Camera characterization methods can help quantify noise, response and dynamic range, but the complete illuminated object still requires application-specific evaluation. [R14]

The preferred illumination arrangement should be selected through comparisons on representative non-biological targets and appropriate plate images. Evaluate not only whether a feature becomes more visible, but whether the resulting measurement remains stable across location, exposure and the permitted range of plate appearance.

pages.title: Environmental and mechanical stability
text: Mechanical and environmental stability determine whether an instrument can reproduce its measurement geometry over time. A stable image requires more than a rigid camera mount: the plate support, focus mechanism, lighting fixture and surrounding thermal conditions can all affect the acquired signal.
## Identify slow and fast disturbances

Slow drift may follow temperature changes, material relaxation or repeated loading. Fast disturbances may arise from fans, motion stages, nearby equipment or contact with the bench. Their signatures differ, so the instrument should not rely on a single generic stability indicator.
## Qualify the assembled instrument

Component specifications do not fully describe the behaviour of the assembly. A low-noise camera mounted on a vibrating structure can still produce unreliable images. A stable temperature sensor at one location does not prove uniform conditions throughout a chamber.

The engineering programme should measure the relationship between disturbances and the quantities that matter to the workflow. If a disturbance has no material effect within the accepted range, it may need only monitoring. If it can invalidate measurement, the response should be explicit: prevent capture, flag affected observations or require requalification. The decision should follow measured sensitivity rather than the mere presence of a sensor.
tables: Verify pose against the permitted geometry and assess scale sensitivity.
Track image quality on a stable reference and control adjustment history.
Compare inertial or image-based evidence with blur and motion artifacts.
Characterize measurement residuals across the intended ambient range.
Record optical obstruction and assess readability instead of assuming a corrective mode works.
Separate electronics cooling requirements from the observation environment.

pages.title: Timing synchronization and acquisition control
text: Time is an essential coordinate in any repeated observation system. The instrument must distinguish the biological event used as a time origin, the start and end of an exposure, the arrival of data and the completion of analysis. These timestamps can differ substantially and should not be collapsed into one “result time.”
## Synchronize the events that need comparison

For multimodal analysis, each observation should identify the interval over which it was measured. A gas sensor may average over seconds while a camera integrates light over milliseconds. Assigning both the same timestamp can create a false impression of simultaneity. Where sensor clocks differ, the synchronization method and estimated timing uncertainty should be recorded.
## Handle clock faults explicitly

A system restart, manual clock correction or loss of synchronization can disrupt ordering. Monotonic counters can help preserve local event sequence, while UTC timestamps support comparison across systems. Both may be useful, but neither should conceal an uncertain biological start time.

Acquisition scheduling should prioritize the observations required by the selected workflow. A missed scheduled image is a missing observation, not an invitation to substitute a generated image into the measured series. Later analysis can model the gap, provided that its status and uncertainty remain explicit. Timing integrity is therefore both an engineering requirement and a condition for credible growth modelling.

pages.title: Sensor selection and information value
text: Sensor selection should begin with a question that the existing observations cannot answer adequately. The relevant comparison is the information gained after accounting for calibration, confounding, maintenance, power and integration. A sensor count is not a measure of diagnostic reliability.
## Compare incremental value

A candidate channel should be assessed against the current baseline using the same records and a prespecified outcome. If it improves a model only because it identifies the acquisition site or experimental batch, it may fail when deployed elsewhere. Its value should persist under tests that separate the intended biological signal from instrument and workflow context.
## Use staged experiments

Begin with instrument characterization and non-biological controls where possible. Then test the assay-specific relationship using suitable reference observations. Finally, evaluate whether the channel improves the complete decision process, including cases in which it is missing or disagrees with other inputs.

The outcome may be to select the sensor, restrict it to research, use it only for instrument quality checks or reject it. A channel that reliably detects a lighting fault may be highly valuable even if it contains no biological information. Conversely, an attractive biological correlation may not justify product integration if it cannot be calibrated or transferred reliably.
tables: Is the measured quantity plausibly connected to the intended question?
Can the channel resolve useful variation within the permitted operating conditions?
Does it add information or repeat the same failure mechanism?

pages.title: Combining modalities without counting votes
text: Multiple sensors can improve observability, but they do not guarantee independent evidence. Two cameras can share the same glare, two temperature sensors can share the same poor placement and several learned models can inherit the same biased training labels. Agreement is useful only when the reasons for possible agreement are understood.
## Model disagreement as information

The proposed fusion system should preserve each channel’s quality state and uncertainty before combining outputs. A disagreement may indicate a sensor fault, timing mismatch, domain shift or a real difference between the quantities being observed. The correct response depends on which of these explanations remains plausible.

A channel that fails its own quality check should be excluded from eligible fusion while its failure record remains. Different quantities require an explicit relationship model, not numerical voting. Independent disagreement should trigger checks of timing, calibration and assumptions. Shared disturbances require common-cause tests and independent references. A missing required channel permits only a separately evaluated degraded mode; otherwise the system should decline the result.
!FIG work/assets/figures/common-cause.png | Shared disturbances can make multiple channels agree incorrectly.
## A simple uncertainty example

For two equally precise estimates with variance σ² and correlation ρ, the variance of their average is σ²(1 + ρ)/2. With zero correlation, averaging can reduce variance. With perfect positive correlation, it does not. This mathematical example concerns uncertainty in comparable estimates; it is not a diagnostic accuracy claim.

The zero-error ambition should therefore become measurable requirements for disagreement detection, fault containment, abstention and recovery. Evaluation should include failures that affect several channels together. The product should be able to explain why a combined result is eligible, which observations contributed and which conditions would invalidate the inference.

pages.title: Using the candidate technology catalogue
text: The following forty entries form a candidate technology catalogue across the platform. They are not an installed sensor list. Some entries describe biological observation methods, some monitor the environment and others assess instrument readiness or control. Several optical entries are related acquisition modes; the catalogue also spans distinct thermal, electrical, chemical, acoustic, mechanical and magnetic principles.
## Read each entry as a selection argument

Each entry identifies the measurable signal, useful question, calibration needs, confounders, integration burden and evidence boundary. A candidate can be well established for measuring a physical quantity while remaining unproven for an AMReye.AI biological application.
## Use the catalogue to narrow choices

Selection should start with the intended assay and the unresolved measurement problem. An environmental channel may help identify an invalid observation without contributing directly to a biological model. A sophisticated spectroscopic channel may require a different sample format and belong in a research instrument rather than Reader V1.

The catalogue deliberately avoids current sensor model names and component generations. The concluding BOM identifies exact candidates for one Reader V1 configuration. That configuration uses only the components needed for its defined endpoint measurement workflow and does not attempt to implement the complete catalogue.

All application proposals require suitable qualification. A literature demonstration is cited where it supports a relevant principle or research precedent; it should not be read as evidence that the proposed AMReye.AI integration has achieved the same result.
